findings.note: match-kind prompts are never fenced: RenderPrompt populates slots for KindMatch (internal/fsm/judge/prompts.go:168-171) without any fenced[] entries, so golden_comment and the candidate finding text are interpolated raw even when Request.Fence is true, while adjudicate and still-present fence the same untrusted values (prompts.go:182,190). This is a prompt-injection surface. It is an explicitly documented, impact-bounded decision, not an oversight: docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-judge-kinds.md:125 states 'match is never fenced' and line 295 bounds the impact (a crafted candidate can claim a golden and skip adjudication, but its own text never propagates) and names product-mode fencing of match as a follow-up. Recorded so the follow-up is not lost.

evidence.note: KindMatch sets slots but no fenced[] entries, so the fence flag is inert for this kind.
Spec records match-unfenced as an accepted, bounded risk with product-mode fencing as a follow-up.

findings.note: RenderPrompt discards format's error: 'user, _ := format(template, values)' at internal/fsm/judge/prompts.go:208. The spec (docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-judge-kinds.md:123) requires a malformed template (lone '}', unknown {slot}) to surface ERR_PROMPT_TEMPLATE, and format does return exactly that (prompts.go:220-243), but the caller drops it and would return an empty user prompt instead of an error. Today the four templates are constants and judge_test.go:159-165 covers format's error paths directly, so nothing is reachable; the gap is that a future template typo fails silently as an empty prompt sent to a paid provider rather than as ERR_PROMPT_TEMPLATE. Not blocking: no current caller can reach it.

evidence.note: format's error is assigned to _ with a comment asserting the templates are constants.

findings.note: memStore's unlock closure is not guarded against a stale or repeated call: it sets r.locked = false unconditionally (internal/fsm/run/store_mem.go:142-146), whereas the JSONL store's unlock deletes the run from s.held and is a no-op on a second call (internal/fsm/run/store_jsonl.go:365-372). A double-unlock, or a stale closure invoked after a later Lock, releases a lock the caller does not hold — a divergence from the file's own claim that MemStore 'behaves exactly like the JSONL store'. Only reachable through caller misuse; the shared store table (store_test.go:44) does not exercise it.

evidence.note: Unlock closure clears r.locked without checking that this closure still owns the lock.
JSONL unlock is guarded by an existence check on s.held, making a repeated call a no-op.

findings.note: judge.Parse routes every unrecognised kind into the still-present branch via 'default:' (internal/fsm/judge/prompts.go:336), while its fail() helper computes the fail-closed decision as 'kind == KindStillPresent' (prompts.go:312), so an unknown kind is parsed with still-present semantics but fails open. The live provider path is safe because RenderPrompt rejects unknown kinds before Parse runs (judge.go:519), but the mock path calls Parse directly on a scripted row's kind (judge.go:666) with no such guard. Low: kinds originate from internal node implementations, not from user-supplied YAML.

evidence.note: default branch treats any unknown kind as still-present rather than returning an error.
Mock path calls Parse(r.Kind, row.Raw) without the RenderPrompt kind validation that guards the live path.
